prod_010:n1.prompt:
You are helping me assemble the full timeline for a resolved incident, using our {{vendor}} incident-management tool, as the first step of running a blameless postmortem.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: the incident ID or name, and confirmation that you're using my configured credentials for {{vendor}}.

Actions to take:
1. Pull the incident record from {{vendor}}, including its status changes, all timestamped updates, alerts, actions taken, and any chat or call notes/decisions logged during the incident.
2. If {{vendor}} exposes a way to find related or similar past incidents (for example, a find-related-incidents lookup), use it to check whether prior incidents provide useful context — related causes, recurring components, or past fixes — and note anything relevant.
3. Compile everything into a single chronological timeline: what was detected, when, by whom/what alert, what actions were taken and by whom, key decisions, and when the incident was mitigated and resolved. Preserve exact timestamps.
4. Flag any gaps or ambiguities in the record (e.g., missing timestamps, unclear ownership of an action) so a human can fill them in during review.
5. If {{vendor}} supports drafting a postmortem or timeline summary from the incident record, generate that draft as a starting point, clearly marked as AI-drafted and needing human review.

Done looks like: a clean, chronological timeline document (with source links back to the original incident record where possible) covering detection through resolution, plus a short list of flagged gaps or open questions, and — if available — a draft postmortem summary attached.

Report back with: the assembled timeline, the list of flagged gaps, a summary of any related past incidents found, and the draft postmortem summary if one was generated. Do not publish, send, or share this outside of preparing it for internal review.

prod_010:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft a blameless postmortem document in {{vendor}} for a recently resolved incident. If you don't already have it, ask me for: the incident name/ID, links or exports from our incident tooling (alerts, chat logs, deploy history) to reconstruct the timeline, and the {{vendor}} workspace/project where this should live.

Actions to take:
1. Using your available {{vendor}} integration and your configured credentials, pull recent activity related to this incident (comments, status changes, linked tasks) to help assemble a chronological timeline of detection, escalation, mitigation, and resolution.
2. Create a new task or page in {{vendor}} to hold the postmortem draft (using the create-task or create-page capability as appropriate for the vendor).
3. Draft the postmortem using a blameless structure: Summary, Timeline, Impact, Root Cause(s), What Went Well, What Went Poorly, Contributing Factors, and a placeholder section for Follow-up Actions (to be filled in during the review). Use neutral, non-blaming language focused on systems and processes, not individuals.
4. Ask {{vendor}}'s AI assistant to generate or refine a status-update-style summary from recent activity to seed the Summary section, then edit for accuracy.
5. Post the drafted write-up as a comment on the incident's task (or embed it in the new document/page), clearly labeled as a draft pending team review.

Done looks like: a single {{vendor}} doc or task exists containing a complete, timeline-backed, blameless draft ready for the review meeting, with the draft also attached/commented on the original incident task for visibility.

Report back with: the link to the created {{vendor}} document/task, a one-paragraph summary of the incident timeline as drafted, and any gaps or missing information you couldn't source automatically and need from me.

This step is drafting only — do not schedule the review meeting or file follow-up actions; those are separate steps.

prod_010:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for a postmortem review meeting for a recently resolved incident. You cannot attend or run the live discussion yourself — holding the actual meeting remains a human step. Your job is to prepare everything needed so the meeting runs smoothly.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the incident ID or name, links to the incident timeline/tooling (e.g., paging system, chat logs, monitoring dashboards), the draft blameless write-up if one exists, and the list of people who should attend (responders, service owners, any stakeholders).

Then do the following:
1. Pull together a concise pre-read: incident summary, timeline of key events, impact, and current draft root-cause hypotheses, using whatever draft write-up or timeline data I provide.
2. Draft a meeting agenda covering: timeline walkthrough, contributing factors discussion, blameless framing reminder, and follow-up action brainstorming.
3. Prepare a list of open questions or gaps in the timeline that the group should resolve during discussion.
4. Draft a proposed list of attendees and a suggested meeting length based on incident severity.
5. Prepare a template for capturing follow-up actions (owner, description, due date) to be filled in live during the meeting.

Once this package is ready, present it to me as a single organized document (pre-read, agenda, open questions, attendee list, action-item template) for me to review and send out ahead of the meeting.

Done looks like: a complete, ready-to-send meeting packet with no unresolved placeholders, plus a short summary of what's included and what decisions or scheduling I still need to handle myself. Since actually holding the discussion and scheduling attendance is a human step, stop for human sign-off once the packet is ready — do not attempt to run, simulate, or summarize a meeting that hasn't happened yet.

prod_010:n4.prompt:
You are helping me file follow-up actions from a completed incident postmortem into our project tracker, {{vendor}}. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the postmortem write-up or incident timeline containing the list of corrective actions discussed in the review, (2) the target {{vendor}} project/list/team identifier where these should be filed, and (3) confirmation that you have configured credentials for {{vendor}}'s API.

Once you have the inputs, do the following:
1. Extract each distinct follow-up action from the postmortem notes, including a clear description of the corrective work.
2. For each action, determine (or ask me to confirm) an owner and a due date — do not leave these blank.
3. Using {{vendor}}'s documented public API, create one task/issue per follow-up action in the specified project/list, setting the title, description (linking back to the postmortem doc if a URL is available), assignee, and due date fields.
4. If {{vendor}} supports automatic triage/prioritization rules or event-triggered actions, check whether a suitable rule already exists for postmortem follow-ups; if not, just proceed with manual creation rather than inventing new automation.
5. After creation, verify each task was successfully created by reading it back via the API (or listing tasks in that project) and confirm owner, due date, and description are correctly set.

Done looks like: every corrective action from the postmortem exists as a task/issue in {{vendor}} with an owner and due date, and no items were skipped or duplicated.

Report back with a list of the created tasks, including their titles, assigned owners, due dates, and any {{vendor}} task/issue links or IDs, plus a note of any actions where an owner or due date could not be determined and needs my input.

prod_010:n5.prompt:
You are helping me publish the public status-page write-up and customer comms for a recently resolved incident, using our {{vendor}} incident-management account (I'll provide login/API access via my configured credentials).

Before starting, ask me for anything missing:
- The incident ID/name in {{vendor}} and a link to its internal timeline or postmortem draft
- The customer-facing severity/impact summary (what broke, who was affected, when)
- Whether this is a new public incident post or an update to an existing one on our status page
- Any specific subscriber groups (customers vs internal stakeholders) that need notifying
- Our house style for public comms (tone, level of technical detail allowed)

Then do the following:
1. Pull the resolved incident's timeline and key facts from {{vendor}}.
2. Draft a blameless, customer-facing write-up: what happened, customer impact, resolution, and any follow-up commitments — using plain language, no internal jargon or blame.
3. Prepare the status-page entry in {{vendor}} (title, affected components, timeline of public-facing updates, final resolution note) as a draft, not yet published.
4. Prepare the subscriber notification content (for customers subscribed to the public status page, and separately for internal stakeholders who subscribe to structured updates without joining the war room), matching {{vendor}}'s notification channels.
5. Confirm the custom domain and branding settings on the public status page look correct if applicable.
6. Compile a short checklist showing: draft write-up text, draft notification text, target audiences, and any open questions or missing facts.

Publishing the status page and sending customer notifications is an external communication that affects customers and our public record, so after preparing everything, stop for human sign-off — do not publish the status page or send any notifications yourself.

Report back with: the drafted write-up, the drafted notifications, the checklist, and a clear note that this is ready for review and manual publish/send.
